parole.significato: A peddler, a huckster, a person who sells easily transportable goods.
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Low German or Dutch, from Middle Low German hoker and ultimately from the root of huckster.

parole.significato: A peddler or hawker, who sells small items, either door-to-door, from a stall, or in the street.
parole.testo: From Middle English hukster, probably of Low German or Dutch origin, from Middle Low German höken (“to peddle”) or Middle Dutch hokester, itself from hoeken (“to peddle, bend, bear on the back”), all from Proto-Germanic *huk-, probably related to *hūkan- (“to squat”), from *hūkkan-, back-formed from

parole.significato: A case of canvas or leather, for carrying items on the back.
parole.testo: From Low German knapzak or Dutch knapzak (older form cnapsack), from Middle Dutch cnappen (“to bite with teeth”), ultimately from knappen (“to eat, crack”), of imitative origin, + sack. German Knappsack is from Dutch.

parole.significato: To sniff or smell with the nose loudly and audibly.
parole.testo: Probably from Low German and Dutch snuffelen (“to snuffle”), equivalent to snuff + -le. Compare also Old English snofl (“snot, nasal mucus”), which might not have survived into Middle English.

parole.significato: A shelf set into a mineshaft for storing waste material, or for use as a step or support.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Low German Stempel or Dutch stempel, akin to Old English stempan (“to stamp”), all from Proto-West Germanic *stampōn, from Proto-Germanic *stampōną (“to compress, squeeze, stamp”).

parole.significato: A native or inhabitant of British America or, later, the United States.
parole.testo: Mid-1700s, from Yankee ("derogatory, American colonist") doodle ("fool") dandy ("foppish or vain man"), the chorus of the eponymous song. parole.significato: A small ship's boat, usually rowed by four or six oars.
parole.testo: Apparently from Low German and Middle Low German jolle, or Dutch jol, possibly ultimately from a Proto-Germanic derivative of Proto-Indo-European *h₂ewlos (“tube”), see also Lithuanian aulas, Norwegian aul, Hittite [script needed] (auli-, “tube-shaped organ in the neck”), Albanian hollë, Latin alvus
